1.why: MFA routes go through owner()/pendingOwner(), which bind the session’s user id to accountIds and never accept an external account identifier.

2.why: TOTP is derived from the account’s own encrypted secret and backup codes are verified only against that account’s hashes, so a code does not authenticate any other user.

3.why: Confirming MFA sets a.mfa=true on the account but does not invalidate or re-challenge any other existing auth-phase sessions.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored with AES-256-GCM (enc/dec) and backup codes are stored as PBKDF2 hashes with per-code salt and pepper.

5.why: Secrets, session ids, CSRF tokens, backup codes, and OTPs are produced with node:crypto randomBytes/randomInt.

6.why: The session cookie is HttpOnly and the client never writes secrets, OTPs, or tokens to localStorage/sessionStorage or non-HttpOnly cookies.

7.why: Email is normalized/regex-checked server-side, OTP/recovery input is constrained by strict patterns, and body size/type are limited.

8.why: UI text is applied via textContent, API data is JSON, and a nonce-based CSP blocks inline script injection.

9.why: The handler never issues redirects or Location headers, so no open-redirect path exists.

10.why: headers() sets CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options DENY, and frame-ancestors 'none' on responses.

11.why: sessionCookie() sets HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict on the MFA session cookie.

12.why: Demo mock identity codes, mock OTPs, and backup codes are written to the browser console and returned in JSON, so they are not kept fully out of logs/output.

13.why: Identity codes are marked used and time-limited; TOTP steps are recorded in usedTotp/used sets; backup codes flip used and carry expires.

14.why: recordFailure/checkLimit lock accounts and sources after repeated failures for LOCK duration, returning 429.

15.why: signin/verify and mfa/verify delete the old session and issue a new id; idle/absolute timeouts expire sessions; logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
